hints: When two characters cancel, their neighbours become neighbours. Which character must you compare each new character with?
Stack simulation: keep surviving characters on a stack. A new character cancels with the top if they are the same letter in different case, which in ASCII means Math.abs(a - b) == 32.

1. Use a StringBuilder sb as a stack.
  2. For each char c: if sb is not empty and |last - c| == 32, remove the last char.
  3. Otherwise append c.
  4. Return sb.toString().

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Scan for any cancelling pair, delete it, and restart until no pair exists.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: One pass with a stack; cancel against the top.

explain: For "mNnMk": push m, push N. Then n and N differ only in case, so pop → [m]. Then M cancels with m → []. Finally push k. The answer is "k". The invariant: no two neighbours on the stack cancel each other. The 32 check works because lowercase and uppercase forms of the same letter are exactly 32 apart in ASCII, while two equal characters (difference 0) do not cancel.
recognize: Neighbouring pairs cancel and the string closes up → stack of survivors.
